title: Node-based latency pathfinder: explainer map visuals for onboarding quickstart
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a set of onboarding-friendly explainer visuals that show how Redwood routes requests by region and latency using a node/pathfinder metaphor. Deliverables: 1) a 3-frame hero diagram (overview -> path selection -> failover) suitable for the Quickstart doc and product tour, 2) two map tile variants (simplified world map and single-region zoom), 3) SVG micro-animations for the console tour showing path switching when latency spikes, and 4) cropped screenshots for the Quickstart page and release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Three final hero frames exported as PNG and SVG at 2x and 3x sizes
Two map tile variants provided: world-simplified.svg and region-zoom.svg with labeled nodes and latency badges
Micro-animation prototypes in Figma demonstrating path switch and fallback (looping .gif or mp4)
Accessibility review: color contrast passes WCAG AA for all overlays and badges
Design token list for engineering handoff (colors, spacing, icon IDs) included in attachments
One console-ready screenshot showing the routing explainer inside the Quickstart modal with copy approved by PM
design_notes: Metaphor: 'nodes' (circles) represent available inference clusters, 'paths' show routing decisions computed by policy (latency-first shown with blue path), 'dashed' path indicates fallback or cross-region failover.
Prefer rounded nodes and pill-shaped latency badges to match Redwood Console visual language.
Badge copy: use compact numbers (e.g., 18 ms) and an optional small chevron to indicate trending (↑ or ↓).
Animations should be subtle and quick (300-450ms) for path switch; not continuous motion to avoid distraction in docs.
Map styling: simplified landmass, muted gray base, use two accent colors: teal for primary route, amber for fallback. Avoid red as primary—reserve for errors.
Zoomed region tile should include labels for 'nearest PoP', 'secondary PoP', and 'fallback region' and approximate latency bands as translucent rings.
Provide a grayscale variant for print-friendly or dark-mode inverted usage.
Include a small keyboard-accessible transcript for the micro-animation describing the switch for screen-reader users.
mockup_variants: Variant A - Hero triptych: Overview (all nodes visible) -> Select path (highlight primary path) -> Failover (primary path fades, fallback path highlights)
Variant B - Single progressive map: a single canvas that highlights nodes in sequence with numbered callouts (1 request arrives, 2 route selected, 3 fallback)
Variant C - Minimal map tile for inline docs: single-region with two nodes, latency badge, and tiny copy line
ux_copy_options: Option 1: 'Redwood routes each request to the best-performing cluster based on latency and policy. If latency increases, requests automatically fail over to the next best region.'
Option 2: 'Requests prefer nearby clusters to minimize latency. When capacity or latency degrades, Redwood gracefully shifts traffic to maintain availability.'
Tooltip short: 'Routing policy: latency-first — preferred node selected automatically.'
engineering_handoff: Export specs: SVG icons as symbol IDs, provide a spritesheet for nodes with states (idle/active/fallback/error).
Give example JSON snippet for console placement (static image + micro-animation fallback) in attachments (see GitHub PR).
Recommend lazy-loading SVG for the Quickstart modal to avoid initial bundle impact; preload hero PNG for first paint.
